understanding.goal_understanding: Progress through each KA59 level by positioning all selectable pieces onto the goal tiles marked '+' at the same time; a level is only won when every goal tile is occupied simultaneously, and the full game is won after the final level reports WIN within the per-level step budget.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each turn you control one currently selected piece ('P') and can MOVE in four directions on a grid where each cell corresponds to 3 pixels; movement attempts to shift the selected piece one cell, but may be blocked or altered by walls/boundaries and other objects. Some adjacent objects (blocks) are pushable and can be moved along in the direction of travel if space allows; walls typically prevent motion/pushing, though different wall-like boundaries can behave inconsistently and require experimentation. If multiple selectables exist, you can switch control using CLICK by providing the exact pixel-coordinate position of the target selectable ('S') from the state; the movement.*_blocked flags are only hints that something is adjacent and do not guarantee the move will fail.

understanding.goal_understanding: Progress through each KA59 level by positioning all selectable pieces onto the goal tiles marked '+' at the same time; a level is only won when every goal tile is occupied simultaneously, and the full game is won after the final level reports WIN within the per-level step budget.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each turn you control one currently selected piece ('P') and can MOVE in four directions on a grid where each cell corresponds to 3 pixels; movement attempts to shift the selected piece one cell, but may be blocked or altered by walls/boundaries and other objects. Some adjacent objects (blocks) are pushable and can be moved along in the direction of travel if space allows; walls typically prevent motion/pushing, though different wall-like boundaries can behave inconsistently and require experimentation. If multiple selectables exist, you can switch control using CLICK by providing the exact pixel-coordinate position of the target selectable ('S') from the state; the movement.*_blocked flags are only hints that something is adjacent and do not guarantee the move will fail.
